一句话：让高层上下文更新频率降低、按需重配底层 MoE，14 个 Atari 游戏上 0.884 HNS，参数与算力都更省。

要点：

  • 高层上下文走跨步（strided）通道，降低全局上下文更新频率，从源头抑制复合漂移的传播
  • 上下文感知路由让门控网络同时看全局上下文与当前观测，动态重配底层 MoE，缓解静态层级里的高低层干扰
  • 77M 参数在 14 个 Atari 子集（10% 离线数据）上取得 0.884 IQM 人类归一化分数，超过同配的 JOWA-70M（0.529），与 JOWA-150M 相当但每序列训练 FLOPs 少 70.88%

为什么值得看：世界模型当训练场时，开环 rollout 的漂移直接决定想象出来的经验可不可信；这条「降低高层更新频率」的工程手段比加结构简单得多。

中文摘要：自回归世界模型是样本高效决策的强范式，但开环 rollout 往往漂移越来越大，即使规划视野不长也会误差累积。层级时间抽象本来是缓解手段——缩短有效预测长度，可现有层级设计会引入额外的结构与概念复杂度，有时反而不好控、对平坦基线的增益也有限。MHWA 的做法很克制：用一条跨步的高层上下文通道降低全局上下文的更新频率，从源头压住复合漂移的传播；再用上下文感知路由，让门控网络同时依据全局上下文与当前观测动态重配底层专家混合，从而灵活协调高低层、缓解静态层级里常见的高低层干扰。在 14 个 Atari 游戏子集、仅用 10% 离线数据的设定下，77M 参数的 MHWA 在三个训练种子上取得 0.884 的 IQM 人类归一化分数，超过同配的 JOWA-70M（0.529），并与 JOWA-150M 数值相当，而每序列训练 FLOPs 少 70.88%。

主题：延伸阅读

来源：arXiv·世界模型+游戏（English）

原文发布：2026-10-10

本期推送：2026-10-25

MHWA: Multi-timescale
Hierarchical World-Action Model

Abstract

Autoregressive world models have emerged as a powerful paradigm for sample efficient decision making, yet their open loop rollouts often exhibit increasing drift that leads to error accumulation even within a relatively small planning horizon. Hierarchical temporal abstraction is a natural candidate to mitigate such drift by reducing the effective prediction horizon; however, existing hierarchical designs can introduce added structural and conceptual complexity, sometimes making them difficult to control and limiting gains over flat baselines. To this end, we introduce MHWA (Multi-timescale Hierarchical World-Action model), which employs a strided high level context channel to reduce global context update frequency, effectively curbing the propagation of compounding drift. Crucially, via context aware routing, the gating network dynamically reconfigures a low level mixture of experts by using both global context and current observations, thereby enabling flexible high–low coordination, helping alleviate interference commonly observed in static hierarchies. Empirically, using RLiable’s seed-by-game aggregation, MHWA (77M parameters) achieves an IQM human normalized score (HNS) of 0.884 across three training seeds on a 14-game Atari subset using 10% subsampled offline data, outperforming a matched JOWA-70M baseline (0.529) and achieving numerically comparable performance to JOWA-150M while using nearly half the parameters and 70.88% fewer training FLOPs per sequence.

1 Introduction

Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (MBRL) offers a promising avenue for sample efficient learning by enabling agents to plan within a learned World Model (WM) [1, 2]. However, maintaining predictive consistency under multi-step open loop rollouts remains a fundamental challenge. State-of-the-art approaches predominantly employ autoregressive Transformer architectures [3, 4, 5]. While effective at short range prediction, autoregressive rollouts can exhibit increasing drift with rollout depth: once the model conditions on its own imperfect predictions, small local errors may compound under distribution shift, causing imagined trajectories to deviate from the real dynamics [6, 7].

A prevalent response to this challenge is to scale model capacity, since larger models can better absorb heterogeneity and noise. A prominent example is the Jointly-Optimized World-Action (JOWA) model, which scales up to 150 million parameters to achieve strong performance in multi-game offline reinforcement learning [5]. While effective, such brute force scaling can be computationally costly, requiring substantial GPU resources and long training cycles, which raises the barrier to iteration.

Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) provides an alternative design axis by introducing temporal abstraction [8, 9]. This motivates the emerging line of Hierarchical Model-Based RL (HMBRL), or Hierarchical World Models (HWM) [10], which aim to separate slow varying context from fast local dynamics and thereby reduce the effective horizon over which global consistency must be maintained. In principle, such multi-timescale structure could improve longer range credit assignment and planning while retaining the sample efficiency benefits of world models.

However, the HWM landscape remains relatively sparse compared to model free approaches; as noted by [Schiewer et al. [10]], combining hierarchy and world modeling often yields systems that are “highly complex and difficult to control,” and the added hierarchy does not reliably outperform flat baselines. A key reason is that existing designs face two coupled forms of interference.

Conceptual (semantic) interference. In many goal conditioned hierarchical formulations, higher-level decisions (e.g., subgoals) are evaluated through the evolving competence of the lower-level goal-reaching policy. As multiple levels learn simultaneously, the semantic meaning and value of a high-level decision can drift over training, inducing a moving target learning signal and exacerbating non-stationarity [11, 10]. This instability is especially pronounced when the abstract interface is high-dimensional or when the hierarchy relies on objectives whose targets implicitly change as the lower level improves.

Structural interference. A second issue is architectural: many hierarchical agents rely on a single universal low-level network conditioned on goals, forcing one set of parameters to fit heterogeneous behaviors and dynamics regimes. Such heavy parameter sharing can entangle incompatible modes and lead to gradient competition across subtasks [11]. This motivates modular parameterizations that can specialize while remaining scalable.

Together, these observations suggest that without explicit decoupling and flexible coordination, simply adding hierarchy can introduce complexity that becomes a burden rather than a benefit.

To address these challenges, we propose the Multi-timescale Hierarchical World Action model (MHWA), a problem structured hierarchical world action model for reducing compounding errors. MHWA treats hierarchy not as a standalone remedy, but as a design that must explicitly control the interference it introduces: slow context inference is decoupled from native resolution local dynamics, and low-level computation is dynamically routed through context aware experts.

Scope. We treat multi-timescale abstraction and context driven routing as an engineering hypothesis for reducing open loop drift under heterogeneous multi-game dynamics, and provide a supporting error bound intuition in Appendix C. Our claims are scoped to multi-game offline Atari, which we use as a controlled benchmark for testing whether structural inductive bias can improve rollout stability without relying solely on brute force scaling.

Our contributions are summarized as follows:

An interference aware hierarchy for reducing compounding errors. We propose MHWA, a problem structured hierarchical world action model that treats hierarchy not as a standalone remedy, but as a mechanism that must be carefully decoupled. Our central hypothesis is that temporal abstraction can mitigate compounding errors in autoregressive world models when conceptual interference between hierarchy levels and structural interference across dynamics modes are explicitly addressed. MHWA implements this idea by coupling slow context inference with native resolution local dynamics through a strided High-Level Manager and a context routed Low-Level Worker.

Isolated slow context learning for conceptual interference. The High-Level Manager learns a slow varying latent context using a skip step predictive objective (L_high), while gradients from low-level losses are blocked before reaching the manager. This prevents the high-level context from being driven by low-level noise or moving target optimization signals.

Context aware expert routing for structural interference. The Low-Level Worker replaces a monolithic feed forward parameterization with a sparsely activated MoE. Its gate conditions jointly on the broadcast high-level context and the instantaneous token state, enabling expert selection to be both mode aware and locally reactive under heterogeneous multi-game dynamics.

Structure versus scale under a controlled benchmark. On a 14-game Atari subset with 10% subsampled offline data, MHWA (77M) achieves an IQM HNS of 0.884 across three training seeds, outperforming JOWA-70M (0.529) trained on the same data with the same batch setting. Its performance is numerically comparable to the published JOWA-150M result (0.833) [5], with nearly half the parameters and 70.88% fewer forward+backward FLOPs per training sequence.

2 Related Work

Offline RL, world models, and compounding errors. Offline RL learns policies from fixed datasets, where distribution shift between the behavior data and the learned policy is a central challenge [12, 13]. Model-free methods often mitigate this issue through policy constraints or conservative value estimation [14, 15, 16], while model-based methods learn dynamics models for planning or policy improvement [17, 18]. World models provide a natural interface for model-based decision making [19, 20]. Recent sequence modeling approaches, including Decision Transformer, IRIS, and JOWA, cast RL as autoregressive prediction over observation-action histories [21, 4, 5]. However, when such models roll out open loop and condition on their own predictions, local errors can compound over time. MHWA targets this failure mode by introducing temporal abstraction into tokenized world action modeling.

Temporal abstraction and conceptual interference. Hierarchical RL decomposes behavior across temporal scales through options, managers, or subgoals [8, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26]. Hierarchical world models similarly aim to separate slow varying context from fast local dynamics [10, 27, 28]. This separation is appealing for reducing effective rollout horizon, but it can also introduce conceptual interference: high-level decisions may be evaluated through a lower-level policy whose competence and semantics evolve during training [11, 10]. THICK [29] learns temporal abstraction from sparse latent context changes and predicts future latent scenarios associated with those changes. In contrast, MHWA uses a fixed strided manager with skip step observation token supervision and stop-gradient-isolated context broadcast, avoiding direct dependence of the high-level context on low-level optimization signals. Beyond temporal abstraction, perturbation-based local learning has also been explored to improve training scalability and convergence efficiency in spiking neural networks [30].

Modularity and structural interference. A second challenge is structural interference, where heterogeneous behaviors or dynamics regimes are forced through a heavily shared low-level parameterization [11]. Sparse Mixture-of-Experts models address a related problem by routing inputs to a subset of specialized parameters [31, 32, 33]. MoE world models support modular dynamics modeling for multi-task and multi-agent learning and planning [34, 35]. MHWA differs by coupling sparse routing with an explicit high-level context channel: the worker gate conditions jointly on the broadcast slow context and the instantaneous token state, enabling expert selection to be both mode aware and locally reactive. Thus, we do not claim skip step prediction, hierarchy, or MoE routing as standalone novelties; our contribution is an interference aware integration of these mechanisms for reducing drift in tokenized multi-game offline world-action modeling.

3 The Multi-timescale Hierarchical World-Action Model (MHWA)

We propose the Multi-timescale Hierarchical World Action model (MHWA), an asymmetric dual-layer architecture for reducing compounding errors in tokenized autoregressive world models. MHWA targets two interference modes: conceptual interference between hierarchy levels, and structural interference across heterogeneous dynamics modes. It addresses the former by isolating a slow high-level context through gradient detachment, and the latter by using context-aware sparse routing in the low-level dynamics model.

3.1 Problem Formulation

We consider offline reinforcement learning as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) M=⟨S,A,ℙ,ℝ,γ⟩. In visual RL, the agent observes high-dimensional observations oₜ∈O rather than ground-truth states, and we treat the stacked observation history as the state representation. Given a static dataset D={τᵢ}ᵢ₌₁^N, where τ=(o₁,a₁,r₁,…,o_T,a_T,r_T), the goal is to learn predictive transition and outcome models that support long-term return maximization.

Following tokenized world-action models, each observation is encoded into K discrete visual tokens using a VQ-VAE tokenizer, reusing the pretrained tokenizer from JOWA. These visual tokens are interleaved with executed action tokens to form a single autoregressive sequence. Token, positional, and task embeddings are combined before both Transformers, retaining JOWA’s explicit task conditioning. An autoregressive predictor processes this sequence and produces embeddings consumed by four heads: (i) a next-observation token head pₒ, (ii) a reward head pᵣ, (iii) a termination head p_d, and (iv) a Q-value head h_Q trained with offline TD learning. In MHWA, this predictor is implemented by the Low-Level Worker modulated by the High-Level Manager, as described in Sec. 3.2. We refer to the components producing (pₒ,pᵣ,p_d) as the world-part and those producing h_Q as the action-part; both world-modeling and TD/CQL critic losses back-propagate through the autoregressive predictor.

Standard autoregressive world models treat trajectories as uniform token sequences, where prediction errors may accumulate with rollout depth. MHWA instead introduces temporal abstraction to infer global context less frequently, while preserving local dynamics prediction at the native token resolution.

3.2 Asymmetric Dual-Layer Architecture

MHWA is organized around the two interference modes above. To mitigate conceptual interference, the high-level representation should capture slow-varying context without being dominated by low-level reconstruction noise. To mitigate structural interference, the low-level model should avoid fitting heterogeneous dynamics with a single shared feed-forward parameterization. Accordingly, MHWA retains the tokenized world-action interface and standard prediction heads, while replacing the monolithic autoregressive predictor with an asymmetric two-level hierarchy (Figure 1): (i) a High-Level Manager that infers slowly varying context at a reduced update frequency, and (ii) a Low-Level Worker implemented as an autoregressive Transformer whose feed-forward sublayers are replaced by sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers. The worker output drives the world-model heads (pₒ,pᵣ,p_d) and the critic head (h_Q). The manager provides an isolated slow context channel, while the worker combines this context with the instantaneous state for dynamic expert routing. This couples temporal abstraction with modular local prediction, directly targeting conceptual and structural interference in heterogeneous multi-game dynamics.

3.3 High-Level Manager: Context Inference

The High-Level Manager targets conceptual interference by learning a slow context representation on a strided temporal scale. Let xₜ∈ℝᵈ denote the input embedding at atomic step t, where xₜ represents either an observation (oₜ) or an action (aₜ) embedding because the input sequence interleaves observations and actions. We introduce a high-level index m, where each step corresponds to atomic timestamp t=1+m·k with stride factor k; we set k=4. At coarse step m, the manager consumes the strided token sequence X⁽ᵐ⁾_slow=(x₁,x₁₊ₖ,…,x_1+m·k), a k-fold temporal downsampling of the atomic sequence. A causal Transformer encoder [36] computes:

hʰⁱᵍʰₘ=Transformer_High(X⁽ᵐ⁾_slow)

(1)

From hʰⁱᵍʰₘ, a trainable Context Projector produces a continuous context vector zᶜᵗˣₘ=Projector(stopgrad(hʰⁱᵍʰₘ)), which parametrizes the slow-varying context of the current dynamics regime rather than acting as a discrete subgoal.

Context Broadcasting and Gradient Isolation. We broadcast zᶜᵗˣₘ to the Low-Level Worker and hold it constant for the subsequent window of k atomic steps. Stop-gradient is placed between the manager and the Context Projector, leaving the projector, router, and worker trainable under the low-level objectives. Thus, the manager is trained through its own auxiliary objective instead of low-level gradients, preventing short-range prediction noise from overwriting the high-level context. This is the main mechanism for controlling conceptual interference between hierarchy levels.

Implementation of Stride. Temporal abstraction is implemented as a fixed token-level stride on the interleaved sequence. This matches the tokenized world-action interface, where visual and action tokens are flattened into one stream. The stride shortens the manager sequence for efficient slow-context inference, while the Low-Level Worker still handles fine-grained native-resolution prediction. Although striding discards some tokens, VQ-VAE visual codes contain sufficient redundancy for coarse context inference.

Distinction from Static Execution. The stride k sets the manager’s temporal sampling and prediction scale; the context-refresh interval r is set to k by default. Unlike static temporal abstractions [10] that lock low-level policies or dynamics for fixed intervals, MHWA keeps the low-level routing mechanism operating at the atomic timescale t. The worker therefore remains locally reactive by conditioning on both the broadcast context and the instantaneous state.

3.4 Low-Level Worker: Context-Aware Dynamic Routing

The Low-Level Worker targets structural interference. In heterogeneous multi-game dynamics, a monolithic low-level FFN must model diverse visual patterns, action effects, and transition modes with shared parameters, which can entangle incompatible behaviors. MHWA replaces these FFN sublayers with sparse MoE layers [31, 32]. The routing mechanism conditions on both the broadcast high-level context and the instantaneous token state, allowing expert selection to reflect slow dynamics modes while remaining locally reactive.

Let xₜ denote the intermediate token representation in the residual stream at token position t, and let zᶜᵗˣₘ be the broadcast high-level context for m=⌊(t-1)/k⌋. A gating projection W_g∈ℝ^2d×N maps the concatenated input to routing logits:

lₜ=(xₜ⊕zᶜᵗˣₘ)W_g,

(2)

where ⊕ denotes concatenation and N is the number of experts {Eⱼ}ⱼ₌₁^N. We apply Top-K sparse routing by selecting Tₜ=TopK(lₜ,Kᵣₒᵤₜₑ) and computing masked Softmax weights. We set N=4; Kᵣₒᵤₜₑ=2:

w_t,j=(\exp(l_t,j))/(∑_r∈Tₜ\exp(l_t,r)), j∈Tₜ; w_t,j=0, j∉Tₜ.

(3)

The MoE output is:

yₜ=xₜ+∑_j∈Tₜw_t,j Eⱼ(xₜ).

(4)

Conditioning the gate on both zᶜᵗˣₘ and xₜ makes routing both mode-aware and locally reactive: the context term encourages specialization across slow-varying dynamics regimes, while the state term preserves sensitivity to instantaneous visual and action-dependent details. This addresses structural interference by replacing a single shared low-level transformation with sparse, context-conditioned expert computation. We use no capacity factor, token dropping, or truncation; all selected tokens are computed, and expert collapse is mitigated with an auxiliary load-balancing regularizer. We provide complete architectural and routing implementation details in Appendix B.

3.5 Learning Objectives

We train the MHWA architecture jointly but with cross-level stop-gradient. Accordingly, the total objective function comprises four distinct components. The first two (L_base,L_critic) are adopted from baseline JOWA [5]. The latter two (L_high,Lₐᵤₓ) are novel structural constraints introduced by MHWA, specifically designed to enforce hierarchical representation learning and dynamic expert specialization.

1. Base World Model Objectives (L_base): Following standard autoregressive approaches, the Low-Level Worker transforms the input sequence into a final hidden representation hₜ. This representation is then used to predict the next discrete observation token oₜ₊₁, reward rₜ, and termination signal dₜ via standard Cross-Entropy loss. This ensures the model accurately simulates the environment’s local dynamics:

L_base=-∑ₜ[\logpₒ(oₜ₊₁|hₜ) (Observation)+\logpᵣ(rₜ|hₜ) (Reward)+\logp_d(dₜ|hₜ) (Termination)](5)

2. Offline Critic Objectives (L_critic): For policy evaluation, we employ a distributional Q-function learned via Temporal Difference (TD) learning, augmented with a Conservative Q-Learning (CQL) penalty to mitigate value overestimation in offline regimes [15]. The critic loss is defined as:

L_critic=L_TD(θ_Q)+α_cqlL_CQL(θ_Q)

(6)

where L_TD minimizes the distributional Bellman error (using C51) and L_CQL penalizes Q-values on out-of-distribution actions.

3. High-Level Representation Learning (L_high): A core challenge in hierarchical modeling is preventing the high-level representation from collapsing into a trivial identity mapping of low-level features or overfitting to transient, hard-to-predict details. To encourage the High-Level Manager to distill slow-varying and semantically meaningful context, we introduce a skip-step predictive objective. Concretely, an MLP projection head p_high predicts the token at the next sampled position using only the corresponding high-level hidden state hʰⁱᵍʰₘ. This skip-step gap acts as an information bottleneck, discouraging reliance on ephemeral noise and promoting representations that remain predictive across multiple token steps:

L_high=-∑ₘ\logpₒʰⁱᵍʰ(o₍ₘ₊₁₎ₖ|hʰⁱᵍʰₘ)

(7)

4. Routing Regularization (Lₐᵤₓ): To prevent expert collapse and ensure balanced resource utilization, we minimize the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between the batch-wise expert selection frequency p̂ and the uniform distribution U:

Lₐᵤₓ=D_KL(p̂∥U)=∑ᵢ₌₁^Nₑₓₚp̂ᵢ\logp̂ᵢ+const

(8)

where p̂ᵢ=(1)/(B·T·Kᵣₒᵤₜₑ)∑_b,tI(i∈T_b,t) represents the normalized selection ratio of expert i within a batch, here B denotes the batch size, T denotes the number of routed token positions per sequence, Kᵣₒᵤₜₑ is the number of active experts per token. Minimizing this objective maximizes the entropy of the routing distribution, enforcing a balanced load across the expert bank.

Total Objective: The final training objective aggregates the main generative tasks with these structural constraints:

Lₜₒₜₐₗ=L_base+L_critic (Main Task)+λₕL_high (Representation)+λₐLₐᵤₓ (Regularization)

(9)

where λₕ and λₐ are hyperparameters governing the strength of the hierarchical and sparsity constraints, respectively. We set λₕ=1, λₐ=0.1.

4 Experiment

4.1 Experimental Setup

Dataset. While previous multi-game offline RL works such as JOWA utilized the DQN Replay Dataset [37], the original source is no longer publicly available. Following the recommendation of the original authors, we utilize the rlu-atari version of the dataset released as part of the RL Unplugged benchmark [38], which maintains the identical data distribution (50M transitions per game per run). However, since the rlu-atari benchmark excludes the game Berzerk, we select a subset of 14 games for training, maintaining the difficulty distribution (easy, medium, hard) [38], see Appendix A. Consistent with [39, 40, 5], we use data from 2 out of 5 training runs. Following the JOWA baseline [5], we uniformly draw 10% of transitions at random, resulting in approximately 10M transitions (including frame stacking) per game.

Training. MHWA has 77.27M total parameters, with 60.49M parameters activated per forward pass. It uses K=36 visual tokens per frame and adopts the same L=8-frame context window as JOWA [5]. We train on 2 NVIDIA A40 GPUs with AdamW [41] and a learning rate of 1×10⁻⁴. To match the baseline token exposure under constrained compute, we use batch size 1024 and 0.875M gradient steps, compared with the published baseline batch size 512 and 1.75M steps. Thus, the total number of processed interaction tokens remains matched. MHWA requires 21.6 GPU-days on 2 A40 GPUs. We compare training computation using forward+backward FLOPs with identical inputs: 8 frames, 296 tokens per sequence, and batch size 256 (Table 2). MHWA uses 42.78% fewer FLOPs per sequence than JOWA-70M and 70.88% fewer than JOWA-150M; the counting details are given in Appendix B.1.

Evaluation and Metrics. We follow the Atari evaluation procedure of JOWA [5], reporting the average return over 16 episodes per game. Performance is measured by Human Normalized Score (HNS), (score-score_random)/(scoreₕᵤₘₐₙ-score_random). For aggregate comparison, we report IQM and Median HNS following RLiable [42].

4.2 Overall Performance Comparison

We compare our method against strong multi-task offline RL baselines, including MTBC, MGDT [39], EDT [43], Scaled-QL [40], and the SOTA model-based approach, JOWA [5]. The baseline results in Table 1 are sourced from the original JOWA paper [5] under the same 10% low-data protocol on the 14 shared games. For MHWA, Table 1 reports the mean and sample standard deviation of seed-level IQMs, while Table 2 reports IQM aggregated across the seed-by-game score matrix. We additionally train JOWA-70M with three independent seeds on the same 14-game rlu-atari dataset and with the same batch setting as MHWA. Using RLiable’s seed-by-game aggregation [42], MHWA-77M achieves IQM HNS 0.884 with a 95% stratified-bootstrap confidence interval of [0.736, 1.031], compared with 0.529 [0.459, 0.602] for the matched JOWA-70M baseline (Table 2). This comparison demonstrates the benefit of the hierarchical routing architecture at comparable model capacity. MHWA is also numerically comparable to the published JOWA-150M result (0.833).

Under the JOWA held-out fine-tuning protocol, MHWA also obtains 0.643±0.007 IQM DNS on five unseen Atari games, close to JOWA-150M (0.647) and above JOWA-70M (0.603); see Appendix E.

4.3 Open-loop Dynamics Modeling

To evaluate error accumulation under autoregressive rollout, we measure open-loop reconstruction quality over steps t=5…8 within the context window. For each game, we sample held-out trajectory segments disjoint from the training data, condition each model on the first four ground-truth frames and corresponding actions, and then roll out from t=5 without injecting ground-truth observations. Actions are kept fixed to the dataset actions, so differences in MSE/PSNR/SSIM against ground-truth frames reflect dynamics-modeling errors rather than policy differences.

As shown in Figure 2, the monolithic JOWA-70M baseline shows a marked deterioration as rollout depth increases, indicating that reducing capacity without architectural changes amplifies error accumulation even within the context window. In contrast, MHWA-77M curbs error propagation and achieves predictive stability comparable to JOWA-150M. A longer-horizon diagnostic from t=5 to t=54 further shows that MHWA outperforms the smaller monolithic baseline and remains comparable to the larger baseline; see Appendix G.

Overall, these results suggest that MHWA improves open-loop stability through structural inductive bias rather than relying solely on brute-force scaling.

4.4 Ablation Studies

We evaluate design choices on a fixed 6-game subset using a 44M MHWA variant (Appendix A). This controlled ablation setting follows the subset-ablation protocol used by JOWA [5] and keeps the study computationally feasible under our available budget. For each variant, we first average the 16 evaluation episodes within each game to obtain one HNS per game, and then compute IQM and Median HNS over the six per-game scores. Table 4 reports the resulting aggregate scores, together with the relative IQM drop compared to the full model. We provide detailed per-game raw scores in Appendix F. To isolate architectural effects from capacity, w/o MoE widens the dense FFN and MoE-only (w/o Manager) widens the experts to keep parameters at ≈44M.

Temporal abstraction. The stride ablations show that the high-level context update frequency is a key factor. Collapsing the hierarchy to k=1 causes the largest degradation among all variants, with a 62.1% relative IQM drop, indicating that temporal abstraction is central to MHWA’s benefit. The default k=4 performs best in this 44M/6-game setting, while k=2 and k=8 remain lower but competitive, with relative IQM drops of 20.9% and 8.3%, respectively. This suggests that insufficient abstraction is especially harmful, whereas overly coarse abstraction has a milder effect in this setting.

Routing mechanism. The MoE-only (w/o Manager) variant removes the manager, Context Projector, skip-step head, and L_high, retaining the task embedding and low-level MoE; its IQM is 0.445. Removing the state input to the router yields IQM 0.359. The larger drop from removing state routing (36.3%) suggests that local state information is especially important for reactive fine-grained prediction. The 21.1% drop from removing the manager pathway further indicates that trajectory-dependent context helps expert selection across slow-varying dynamics modes.

MoE modularity. Replacing the sparse MoE with a dense FFN at matched parameter count (w/o MoE) reduces IQM to 0.450, corresponding to a relative IQM drop of 20.2%. This is consistent with modular specialization being beneficial under heterogeneous multi-game dynamics.

High-level supervision and routing regularization. Removing the skip-step objective L_high yields a moderate drop (IQM: 0.564→0.503, 10.8%), suggesting that explicit high-level supervision helps the manager learn stride-level predictive context rather than short-range noisy features. Removing the load-balancing regularizer Lₐᵤₓ causes a larger drop (IQM: 0.564→0.444, 21.3%), supporting its role in preventing expert collapse and maintaining stable specialization.

Gradient isolation. The completed factorial ablation (Table 3) shows that stop-gradient improves IQM both with L_high (0.533→0.564) and without it (0.387→0.503). Without L_high, the manager has fixed weights but supplies trajectory-dependent hidden states to the trainable Context Projector. Replacing those states with zeros or Gaussian noise reduces IQM from 0.503 to 0.406 or 0.381 (Appendix F.1).

Expert configuration and context refresh. The default four-expert, Top-2 configuration performs best among the tested alternatives; four-expert Top-1 obtains 0.542 and eight-expert Top-2 obtains 0.511 (Appendix F.2). Separating manager stride from context refresh, retraining with k=4,r=2 gives IQM 0.558 versus 0.564 for the default r=4, with Median HNS 0.484 versus 0.463 (Appendix F.3).

4.5 Interpretability of Representation Learning

To probe whether MHWA captures semantically meaningful dynamics, we visualize the PCA-projected expert activation frequencies of the last MoE layer. Assault and Phoenix are both vertical space shooters sharing identical mechanics, and the projection shows that this similarity is reflected in the full MHWA model (Fig. 3a) via highly similar expert-usage patterns. In contrast, this correspondence is not preserved when removing high-level supervision (Fig. 3b) or the temporal stride (Fig. 3c), suggesting that the L_high and time abstraction design is necessary for the model to recover such task-level commonalities from expert activations.

5 Discussion and Conclusion

We introduced MHWA, a multi-timescale hierarchical world-action model that combines a strided, gradient-isolated high-level manager with a context-aware MoE low-level worker. The manager reduces how often global context must be inferred, while the worker remains reactive at the native token resolution and routes computation through specialized experts. On the 10% offline Atari benchmark, MHWA outperforms a matched three-seed JOWA-70M baseline, achieves numerically comparable performance to JOWA-150M with 77M parameters and 70.88% fewer training FLOPs per sequence, and shows competitive adaptation to held-out Atari games.

The current evidence is intentionally scoped. We evaluate primarily in discrete-action offline Atari with a pretrained tokenizer and fixed stride, and extending to adaptive temporal abstraction [44], continuous control, and broader domains remains future work.

（参考文献见原文。）

Appendix A Atari Game Subset

We follow the game difficulty taxonomy introduced in the RL Unplugged Atari benchmark [38] and report the properties of the games used in our multi-game training set. Compared to the 20-game suite reported in prior work, we do not include games used for fine-tuning/transfer evaluation, and we additionally exclude Berzerk because it is not available in the rlu-atari release. The resulting training set contains 14 Atari games, listed in Table 5 along with their difficulty labels and action-space sizes.

6-game subset for ablations.

Following the subset protocol used in JOWA, we conduct ablations on a fixed 6-game subset: Assault, Carnival, Centipede, NameThisGame, Phoenix, and SpaceInvaders. This subset is chosen to keep a reasonably balanced mix of difficulty levels and discrete action-space sizes.

Appendix B Architecture and Parameterization Details

The High-Level Manager is also a 4-layer, 8-head, 512-dimensional Transformer, but uses a dense MLP with expansion ratio 4 instead of MoE. Its output is detached before a trainable 512→512 Context Projector and broadcast across the following stride window. Low-level losses train the Context Projector, router, and worker, while L_high trains the manager. Both Transformers receive the shared token, positional, and task embeddings. The tokenized interface uses 37 tokens per block, consisting of 36 visual tokens and one action token, with 8 blocks per sequence. The critic head uses one Q-head, MLP dimension 768, and dropout 0.01.

The Low-Level Worker is a 4-layer causal Transformer with 8 attention heads and embedding dimension 512. Each feed-forward sublayer is replaced by an MoE layer with N=4 experts and Top-K=2 routing. Each expert is a 512→2048→512 GELU MLP. The routing gate is a bias-free linear projection over the concatenation of the current token state and the broadcast high-level context. We do not use token dropping or capacity truncation; all selected tokens are computed, and exactly two experts are active per token.

The full MHWA model contains 77.27M parameters, with approximately 60.49M parameters activated per forward pass including the tokenizer.

B.1 Training Computation

We count forward+backward FLOPs for the main experimental configurations using 8 frames and 296 tokens per sequence, with batch size 256. The count includes the complete forward graph, world-model, critic, and auxiliary losses, and backward computation. For MHWA, it includes both hierarchy levels, all four MoE layers, four stored experts with Top-2 routing, load balancing, and high-level observation prediction. MoE computation is counted for the activated experts.

Appendix C A Simple Error-Propagation View

We provide a simple formal view of when a strided context model can have a smaller one-step open-loop rollout-error bound than a flat model. This analysis is intended to isolate the core mechanism of MHWA, rather than to provide a general performance guarantee. We focus on open-loop state prediction under a fixed action sequence.

Let the latent state be xₜ=(sₜ,cₜ), where sₜ∈S denotes the fast state and cₜ∈ℂ denotes the slow context. Let A be any metric action space, either discrete or continuous. The true dynamics are

sₜ₊₁=f(sₜ,cₜ,aₜ).

(10)

item.title: 世界模型取代不了游戏引擎：引擎卖「算出来对」，模型卖「看起来像」，是上下游不是换代 ｜ 世界模型 7 讲（七）：它取代不了游戏引擎，但它能替你省掉最贵的那笔试错
item.description:
一句话：用「要对还是要像」一句判据分清分工，并给出净收益公式：省下的试错次数减掉错误代价与接入维护成本。

要点：

  • 引擎与物理仿真器按人写的规则算、可复现、可审计；世界模型从数据里学、擅长多样与快，但误差藏在权重里难追责
  • 腾讯 HY-World 2.0 官方口径的重点是能导出 Mesh / 3DGS / 点云并导入 Unity、UE 二次编辑——把世界模型放在引擎上游而不是替代它
  • 可自己算的净收益 ≈ N × C_real − p × C_err − C_build：试错次数少、错误代价大、接入维护被忽略，这三条任一成立就不划算

为什么值得看：给团队一个能直接用的判断口径：先问这一步要的是「对」还是「像」，再算三笔账，比追榜单分数靠谱。

中文摘要：这是「世界模型 7 讲」的最后一篇，落到边界上。作者先纠正一个流行误解：世界模型不是下一代引擎。引擎与物理仿真器的结果按人写的规则算出来、同一输入跑两次完全一致、出错能查能审计；世界模型从数据里学、擅长多样与快速，但同输入可能不一致、误差藏在权重里。所以判据只剩一句：你要的是「算出来对」，还是「看起来对」。最能说明问题的是厂商自己怎么摆它——腾讯开源 HY-World 2.0 时强调的不是造世界，而是能导出 Mesh、3DGS、点云等格式并直接导入 Unity、UE 做二次编辑，即把世界模型放在引擎上游。文章随后列出已经能用的四块地方（可交互原型、3D 生产与场景重建、具身仿真底座、策略预训练与数据增广），并给出一个可自己算的净收益式子：省下的试错成本减去错误代价，再减去最容易漏掉的接入与维护成本。

主题：延伸阅读

来源：公众号·AI科技温度（中文）

原文发布：2026-10-22

本期推送：2026-10-25

世界模型 7 讲第 7 篇 / 共 7 篇 · 落地边界

七篇之前，我们从一个站在餐桌前的机器人开始：桌上有个白色马克杯，旁边是一瓶没盖盖子的酱油，它练了几千次才学会不洒。

这一篇是最后一篇，回到它。

过去六篇做的事是：把世界模型拆成压缩、学规律、推演三步（D1），让这三步在一个真实案例里从头跑完（D2），指出它到底卡在哪（D3），看各家怎么应对（D4、D5），最后给你一套不看榜单分数也能自己判断的判据（D6）。

机制和判断都说完了，剩下两个最实际的问题：这东西现在能用到哪，以及它做不到什么。

世界模型不是把世界变便宜了，是把"试错"这件最贵的事，从真实世界搬进了模型里。 01

先纠正最后一个误解：它不是游戏引擎的替代品

很多报道把世界模型写成了"下一代引擎"——输入一句话，一个可玩的世界就出来了，美术、关卡、物理全包。

这个说法错在一个地方：引擎和世界模型卖的，不是同一个东西。


游戏引擎 / 物理仿真器世界模型
结果的来源按人写的规则算出来从数据里学出来
同一输入跑两次完全一致，可复现可能不一致
出错了能查吗能，规则是显式的，可审计难，误差藏在权重里
擅长精确、可控、可追责多样、快速、不用人写规则
一句话保证"对"保证"像"

所以真正的判据只有一句：你要的是"算出来对"，还是"看起来对"。

桥梁受力、芯片时序、车辆碰撞的责任认定——要"对"，引擎不可替代。关卡原型、概念设计、机器人策略预训练的数据增广——要"像"，世界模型划算。

最能说明问题的是厂商自己怎么摆它。腾讯 2026-04-16 发布并开源的混元 3D 世界模型 2.0（HY-World 2.0），官方口径里最关键的一句不是"造世界"，而是它支持导出 Mesh / 3DGS / 点云等 3D 资产格式，可直接导入 Unity、UE 做二次编辑，定位是"与现有游戏工作流无缝对接"（腾讯发布口径，央广网、上海证券报 2026-04-16 报道）。

最懂游戏的这家公司，把世界模型放在了引擎的上游，而不是引擎的位置上。

业内也有同样的观察：开发者可以借助世界模型完成游戏 Demo，却仍需使用游戏引擎完善产品（光明网 2026-02-06，参考世界互联网大会综述）。

引擎负责"对"，世界模型负责"多"和"快"。它们是上下游，不是换代关系。 02

已经能用起来的四块地方

第一块：可交互原型与概念验证。

Genie 3（Google DeepMind，2025-08-05 官方博客）：720p、20–24 fps 实时交互（DeepMind 官网模型页口径），支持"可提示的世界事件"——用一句话改变天气、塞进一个物体。2026 年 1 月，DeepMind 以 Project Genie 这一实验性研究原型的形式向部分用户开放（光明网 2026-02-06 报道，面向美国 Google AI Ultra 用户）。

用在哪：把前期概念设计、场景原型、动态分镜预览，从几天压到几分钟。用在哪不行：直接当成品——它官方自己写了五条局限，见第 04 节。

第二块：3D 生产与场景重建。

World Labs（李飞飞创办）第一款产品 Marble，生成可漫游、可编辑、可导出的 3D 世界；2026-09-01 发布 Atlas，官方称为多模态世界模型，1 到 6 张图可生成最长 1 分钟、1440p 的视频，并可由稀疏视角重建三维场景，在 DTU 等公开数据集上重建误差 25.3‰（World Labs 官方口径，财联社《科创板日报》2026-09-02、中国证券报 2026-09-03 报道；厂商自述，未见独立复现），目前向部分合作伙伴开放早期访问。腾讯 HY-World 2.0 的 WorldMirror 2.0 架构也是同一思路：一次预测密集点云、多视角深度、表面法线和相机参数，把真实场景复刻成数字资产。

这里有个共同点值得记住：这两家都在拼"能不能导出成标准 3D 资产"，而不是"能不能生成更长的视频"。因为能不能进生产线，取决于能不能交付给下游工具。

第三块：具身智能的仿真底座。

这是最难也最有价值的一块。可查的实例：DayDreamer（CoRL 2022，arXiv:2206.14176，论文自报）用世界模型让机器狗在约 1 小时真实交互内学会翻身、站立、行走；NVIDIA GR00T-Dreams 称把合成数据生成时间从"近三个月"压到 36 小时（厂商自述，未见独立复现）；World Labs 2026-07-28 提出 R2S2R（Real-to-Sim-to-Real）：把真实场景搬进仿真，在里面训练和评估策略，再回到真实。

第四块：策略预训练与数据增广。

这是第三块的前提，也是目前落地最稳的一块——因为这里对"像"的要求高、对"对"的要求相对低。但要记住一句话：模型造出来的数据分布，来自它见过的真实数据，它是放大器，不是来源。真实数据为零的领域，它也变不出东西。

03

深读：算一笔账，什么时候它才真的划算

一个可以自己算的式子：

净收益 ≈ N × C_real  −  p × C_err  −  C_build

大白话翻译：

  • N × C_real
     是省下来的——本来要在真实世界试 N 次，每次成本 C_real
  • p × C_err
     是赔进去的——模型给了错的建议，概率 p，代价 C_err
  • C_build
     是最容易漏掉的一项——把它接进你的流程、校准、持续维护的成本

    • 三个变量各自对应一个常见陷阱：

  • N
     小、
    C_real
     低（比如线上实验本来就很便宜）→ 省不了多少，别上
  • p
     或 
    C_err
     大（错了会伤人、会赔钱、不可撤销）→ 赔不起，别上
  • C_build
     被忽略（模型很酷，但要人天天盯着调）→ 账最后算不平

    • 把公开的三组数字放进这张表对照（注意口径）：

    场景真实侧模型侧出处与口径
    DayDreamer 机器狗约 1 小时真实交互学会翻身站立行走在模型里规划后执行CoRL 2022，arXiv:2206.14176，论文自报
    GR00T-Dreams"近三个月"36 小时NVIDIA 厂商自述，未见独立复现
    Genie 3 连续交互—数分钟，不是数小时DeepMind 官方局限声明，2025-08-05

    第三行是这张表里最重要的一行，因为它是负面的：目前最强的实时交互世界模型，一次连续交互的天花板是"几分钟"。任何需要长时间连续推演的任务，都会在半途掉出可信区——这正好是 D3 讲的误差累积、D6 讲的多轮衰减，在产品规格上的表现。

    世界模型省的是"次数"，赔的是"信错"。算清这两笔，比看任何一个榜单分数都管用。 04

    诚实清单：它现在做不到什么

    分两类。这比"能做什么"重要得多。

    A. 结构性做不到——不是努力就能补上的，是这套方法本身的代价。

    一是不能当"真相"用。它输出的是学出来的概率性后果，不是按物理定律算出来的确定结果。凡是要签字、要追责、要过认证的场合，它只能当辅助，不能当依据。

    二是不能保证可复现。同一输入两次运行结果可能不同。这在工程上很致命：你没法做回归测试，出了 bug 也没法定位。

    三是长链条推演不可信。误差是相乘不是相加，交互时长以分钟计。

    B. 暂时做不到——DeepMind 在 2025-08-05 官方博客里自己列了五条局限，逐条翻译：

  • 动作空间有限：很多环境干预要靠文本提示触发，不是智能体自己做出来的
  • 多智能体交互：共享环境里多个独立智能体之间的复杂交互，仍是开放问题
  • 真实地理位置：无法以完美地理精度模拟真实地点
  • 文字渲染：通常只有在输入描述里明确给过的字，才能生成清晰文本
  • 交互时长：支持数分钟连续交互，不支持数小时

    • 再补一条来自评测侧的证据：WBench 上 20 个受评模型的平均导航分，从第 1 轮到第 4 轮及以后掉了 33 分（arXiv:2605.25874，2026-05-25 提交，论文自报）。"第一轮惊艳、第四轮露馅"是当前的普遍状态，不是某一家的问题。

    判断它能不能用，最快的办法不是看它能做什么，是看它官方肯承认自己不能做什么。 05

    自己动手：给你的领域做一次"值不值得用"评估

    四个问题，每题给自己打 0 / 1 / 2 分：

    问一：你现在的真实试错，一次代价有多高？ 很低（线上就能试）= 0；中等（要人、要停机）= 1；很高（要真机、有危险）= 2。

    问二：信错了会怎样？ 可撤销 = 0；要返工 = 1；不可逆或伤人 = 2。

    问三：你的任务需要连续推演多久？ 几步之内就做决定 = 0；几十步 = 1；几分钟以上 = 2。

    问四：你有没有便宜的办法验证它的建议？ 有且便宜 = 0；有但贵 = 1；没有 = 2。

    判读：

  • 问一高、问二低、问三低、问四低 → 现在就该试
  • 问二 = 2 → 不管别的多少分，先别用
  • 问三 = 2 → 等一致性再走一步，或者把任务拆短
  • 问四 = 2 → 你没法闭环修正，等于把 C_err 放大

    • 打完分，再用 D6 那三条判据（反事实敏感度、发散速度、规划增益）拿你自己的场景实测一遍。分数是别人的体检，自己摸的那三下才是脉。

    06

    本篇事实清单

  • 已验证（官方原文 / 论文可查）：Genie 3 的技术规格与官方自列五条局限（Google DeepMind 官方博客，2025-08-05）；Project Genie 为实验性研究原型、面向部分用户（DeepMind 2026-01 发布，光明网 2026-02-06 报道）；腾讯 HY-World 2.0 于 2026-04-16 发布并开源、支持导出 Mesh/3DGS/点云并对接 Unity、UE（央广网、上海证券报 2026-04-16 报道）；World Labs Atlas 于 2026-09-01 发布（World Labs 官方博客，中国证券报 2026-09-03 报道）；World Labs R2S2R 于 2026-07-28 发布；DayDreamer（CoRL 2022，arXiv:2206.14176，论文自报）；WBench 多轮衰减 33 分（arXiv:2605.25874，2026-05-25 提交，论文自报）
  • 厂商宣传（未见独立复现）：Atlas 的 1440p / 1 分钟 / 1–6 张图、DTU 重建误差 25.3‰；GR00T-Dreams 的 36 小时 vs 近三个月；HY-World 2.0 的"SOTA 级生成效果"
  • 不清楚：各家世界模型在真实业务流水线中的稳定产出率与人工返工比例（未见到公开数据）；Atlas 面向"部分合作伙伴早期访问"的具体名单与规模；本文不对任何产品的能力演进做预测
    • 07

    写在最后：七篇讲完，回到那个机器人

    把七篇收成一句话：世界模型输出的不是画面，是后果；真正的难题是后果在推演三十步之后还剩多少可信度；而判断它能不能用在你的场景里，看的是省下的试错够不够赔上信错的代价。

    那个倒酱油的机器人，现在可以不用练几千次了——但也不是什么都不练。它变成：在模型里练几百次，在真实世界执行几次，失败了回流修正。真实世界那几次从来没有被取消，只是被缩到了最少。

    这大概是这项技术最诚实的样子：它不消灭真实，它把真实省着用。

    七篇到此结束。最后聊个具体的：如果你的业务要用世界模型，你会把它放在流程的哪一环——最前面做原型、中间做训练数据、还是在决策前做预演？为什么是那一环？ 评论区说说你的理由。

    信源 ① Google DeepMind《Genie 3: A new frontier for world models》官方博客，2025-08-05（720p、24fps、数分钟一致性、可提示的世界事件，及官方自列五条局限）② DeepMind 官网 Genie 3 模型页（20–24 fps 口径）；Project Genie 实验性研究原型，2026-01 向部分用户开放，光明网 2026-02-06 报道 ③ 腾讯《混元 3D 世界模型 2.0（HY-World 2.0）》发布并开源，2026-04-16，央广网、上海证券报、中国证券报报道（Mesh/3DGS/点云导出、对接 Unity/UE、WorldMirror 2.0）④ World Labs《Atlas》官方博客，2026-09-01；财联社《科创板日报》2026-09-02、中国证券报 2026-09-03 报道（1440p、1 分钟、1–6 张图、DTU 重建误差 25.3‰，均为厂商自述）⑤ World Labs R2S2R，2026-07-28 发布 ⑥ Wu Yan 等《DayDreamer: World Models for Physical Robot Learning》，CoRL 2022，arXiv:2206.14176（约 1 小时真实交互，论文自报）⑦ NVIDIA GR00T-Dreams（36 小时 vs 近三个月，厂商自述）⑧ Ying Kaining 等《WBench》，arXiv:2605.25874，2026-05-25 提交（20 个模型导航分 T1→T4+ 下降 33 分，论文自报）
    本文所有能力与规格描述均截至各自发布日期；厂商自述数字未获独立复现，引用时保留口径。本文不对任何产品、模型或榜单的能力演进做预测。 世界模型 7 讲 · 第 7 篇 / 共 7 篇下一篇 → 系列完结。七篇讲完，回到那个倒酱油的机器人
item.content:encoded:
一句话：用「要对还是要像」一句判据分清分工，并给出净收益公式：省下的试错次数减掉错误代价与接入维护成本。

要点：

  • 引擎与物理仿真器按人写的规则算、可复现、可审计；世界模型从数据里学、擅长多样与快，但误差藏在权重里难追责
  • 腾讯 HY-World 2.0 官方口径的重点是能导出 Mesh / 3DGS / 点云并导入 Unity、UE 二次编辑——把世界模型放在引擎上游而不是替代它
  • 可自己算的净收益 ≈ N × C_real − p × C_err − C_build：试错次数少、错误代价大、接入维护被忽略，这三条任一成立就不划算

为什么值得看：给团队一个能直接用的判断口径：先问这一步要的是「对」还是「像」，再算三笔账，比追榜单分数靠谱。

中文摘要：这是「世界模型 7 讲」的最后一篇，落到边界上。作者先纠正一个流行误解：世界模型不是下一代引擎。引擎与物理仿真器的结果按人写的规则算出来、同一输入跑两次完全一致、出错能查能审计；世界模型从数据里学、擅长多样与快速，但同输入可能不一致、误差藏在权重里。所以判据只剩一句：你要的是「算出来对」，还是「看起来对」。最能说明问题的是厂商自己怎么摆它——腾讯开源 HY-World 2.0 时强调的不是造世界，而是能导出 Mesh、3DGS、点云等格式并直接导入 Unity、UE 做二次编辑，即把世界模型放在引擎上游。文章随后列出已经能用的四块地方（可交互原型、3D 生产与场景重建、具身仿真底座、策略预训练与数据增广），并给出一个可自己算的净收益式子：省下的试错成本减去错误代价，再减去最容易漏掉的接入与维护成本。

主题：延伸阅读

来源：公众号·AI科技温度（中文）

原文发布：2026-10-22

本期推送：2026-10-25

世界模型 7 讲第 7 篇 / 共 7 篇 · 落地边界

七篇之前，我们从一个站在餐桌前的机器人开始：桌上有个白色马克杯，旁边是一瓶没盖盖子的酱油，它练了几千次才学会不洒。

这一篇是最后一篇，回到它。

过去六篇做的事是：把世界模型拆成压缩、学规律、推演三步（D1），让这三步在一个真实案例里从头跑完（D2），指出它到底卡在哪（D3），看各家怎么应对（D4、D5），最后给你一套不看榜单分数也能自己判断的判据（D6）。

机制和判断都说完了，剩下两个最实际的问题：这东西现在能用到哪，以及它做不到什么。

世界模型不是把世界变便宜了，是把"试错"这件最贵的事，从真实世界搬进了模型里。 01

先纠正最后一个误解：它不是游戏引擎的替代品

很多报道把世界模型写成了"下一代引擎"——输入一句话，一个可玩的世界就出来了，美术、关卡、物理全包。

这个说法错在一个地方：引擎和世界模型卖的，不是同一个东西。


游戏引擎 / 物理仿真器世界模型
结果的来源按人写的规则算出来从数据里学出来
同一输入跑两次完全一致，可复现可能不一致
出错了能查吗能，规则是显式的，可审计难，误差藏在权重里
擅长精确、可控、可追责多样、快速、不用人写规则
一句话保证"对"保证"像"

所以真正的判据只有一句：你要的是"算出来对"，还是"看起来对"。

桥梁受力、芯片时序、车辆碰撞的责任认定——要"对"，引擎不可替代。关卡原型、概念设计、机器人策略预训练的数据增广——要"像"，世界模型划算。

最能说明问题的是厂商自己怎么摆它。腾讯 2026-04-16 发布并开源的混元 3D 世界模型 2.0（HY-World 2.0），官方口径里最关键的一句不是"造世界"，而是它支持导出 Mesh / 3DGS / 点云等 3D 资产格式，可直接导入 Unity、UE 做二次编辑，定位是"与现有游戏工作流无缝对接"（腾讯发布口径，央广网、上海证券报 2026-04-16 报道）。

最懂游戏的这家公司，把世界模型放在了引擎的上游，而不是引擎的位置上。

业内也有同样的观察：开发者可以借助世界模型完成游戏 Demo，却仍需使用游戏引擎完善产品（光明网 2026-02-06，参考世界互联网大会综述）。

引擎负责"对"，世界模型负责"多"和"快"。它们是上下游，不是换代关系。 02

已经能用起来的四块地方

第一块：可交互原型与概念验证。

Genie 3（Google DeepMind，2025-08-05 官方博客）：720p、20–24 fps 实时交互（DeepMind 官网模型页口径），支持"可提示的世界事件"——用一句话改变天气、塞进一个物体。2026 年 1 月，DeepMind 以 Project Genie 这一实验性研究原型的形式向部分用户开放（光明网 2026-02-06 报道，面向美国 Google AI Ultra 用户）。

用在哪：把前期概念设计、场景原型、动态分镜预览，从几天压到几分钟。用在哪不行：直接当成品——它官方自己写了五条局限，见第 04 节。

第二块：3D 生产与场景重建。

World Labs（李飞飞创办）第一款产品 Marble，生成可漫游、可编辑、可导出的 3D 世界；2026-09-01 发布 Atlas，官方称为多模态世界模型，1 到 6 张图可生成最长 1 分钟、1440p 的视频，并可由稀疏视角重建三维场景，在 DTU 等公开数据集上重建误差 25.3‰（World Labs 官方口径，财联社《科创板日报》2026-09-02、中国证券报 2026-09-03 报道；厂商自述，未见独立复现），目前向部分合作伙伴开放早期访问。腾讯 HY-World 2.0 的 WorldMirror 2.0 架构也是同一思路：一次预测密集点云、多视角深度、表面法线和相机参数，把真实场景复刻成数字资产。

这里有个共同点值得记住：这两家都在拼"能不能导出成标准 3D 资产"，而不是"能不能生成更长的视频"。因为能不能进生产线，取决于能不能交付给下游工具。

第三块：具身智能的仿真底座。

这是最难也最有价值的一块。可查的实例：DayDreamer（CoRL 2022，arXiv:2206.14176，论文自报）用世界模型让机器狗在约 1 小时真实交互内学会翻身、站立、行走；NVIDIA GR00T-Dreams 称把合成数据生成时间从"近三个月"压到 36 小时（厂商自述，未见独立复现）；World Labs 2026-07-28 提出 R2S2R（Real-to-Sim-to-Real）：把真实场景搬进仿真，在里面训练和评估策略，再回到真实。

第四块：策略预训练与数据增广。

这是第三块的前提，也是目前落地最稳的一块——因为这里对"像"的要求高、对"对"的要求相对低。但要记住一句话：模型造出来的数据分布，来自它见过的真实数据，它是放大器，不是来源。真实数据为零的领域，它也变不出东西。

03

深读：算一笔账，什么时候它才真的划算

一个可以自己算的式子：

净收益 ≈ N × C_real  −  p × C_err  −  C_build

大白话翻译：

  • N × C_real
     是省下来的——本来要在真实世界试 N 次，每次成本 C_real
  • p × C_err
     是赔进去的——模型给了错的建议，概率 p，代价 C_err
  • C_build
     是最容易漏掉的一项——把它接进你的流程、校准、持续维护的成本

    • 三个变量各自对应一个常见陷阱：

  • N
     小、
    C_real
     低（比如线上实验本来就很便宜）→ 省不了多少，别上
  • p
     或 
    C_err
     大（错了会伤人、会赔钱、不可撤销）→ 赔不起，别上
  • C_build
     被忽略（模型很酷，但要人天天盯着调）→ 账最后算不平

    • 把公开的三组数字放进这张表对照（注意口径）：

    场景真实侧模型侧出处与口径
    DayDreamer 机器狗约 1 小时真实交互学会翻身站立行走在模型里规划后执行CoRL 2022，arXiv:2206.14176，论文自报
    GR00T-Dreams"近三个月"36 小时NVIDIA 厂商自述，未见独立复现
    Genie 3 连续交互—数分钟，不是数小时DeepMind 官方局限声明，2025-08-05

    第三行是这张表里最重要的一行，因为它是负面的：目前最强的实时交互世界模型，一次连续交互的天花板是"几分钟"。任何需要长时间连续推演的任务，都会在半途掉出可信区——这正好是 D3 讲的误差累积、D6 讲的多轮衰减，在产品规格上的表现。

    世界模型省的是"次数"，赔的是"信错"。算清这两笔，比看任何一个榜单分数都管用。 04

    诚实清单：它现在做不到什么

    分两类。这比"能做什么"重要得多。

    A. 结构性做不到——不是努力就能补上的，是这套方法本身的代价。

    一是不能当"真相"用。它输出的是学出来的概率性后果，不是按物理定律算出来的确定结果。凡是要签字、要追责、要过认证的场合，它只能当辅助，不能当依据。

    二是不能保证可复现。同一输入两次运行结果可能不同。这在工程上很致命：你没法做回归测试，出了 bug 也没法定位。

    三是长链条推演不可信。误差是相乘不是相加，交互时长以分钟计。

    B. 暂时做不到——DeepMind 在 2025-08-05 官方博客里自己列了五条局限，逐条翻译：

  • 动作空间有限：很多环境干预要靠文本提示触发，不是智能体自己做出来的
  • 多智能体交互：共享环境里多个独立智能体之间的复杂交互，仍是开放问题
  • 真实地理位置：无法以完美地理精度模拟真实地点
  • 文字渲染：通常只有在输入描述里明确给过的字，才能生成清晰文本
  • 交互时长：支持数分钟连续交互，不支持数小时

    • 再补一条来自评测侧的证据：WBench 上 20 个受评模型的平均导航分，从第 1 轮到第 4 轮及以后掉了 33 分（arXiv:2605.25874，2026-05-25 提交，论文自报）。"第一轮惊艳、第四轮露馅"是当前的普遍状态，不是某一家的问题。

    判断它能不能用，最快的办法不是看它能做什么，是看它官方肯承认自己不能做什么。 05

    自己动手：给你的领域做一次"值不值得用"评估

    四个问题，每题给自己打 0 / 1 / 2 分：

    问一：你现在的真实试错，一次代价有多高？ 很低（线上就能试）= 0；中等（要人、要停机）= 1；很高（要真机、有危险）= 2。

    问二：信错了会怎样？ 可撤销 = 0；要返工 = 1；不可逆或伤人 = 2。

    问三：你的任务需要连续推演多久？ 几步之内就做决定 = 0；几十步 = 1；几分钟以上 = 2。

    问四：你有没有便宜的办法验证它的建议？ 有且便宜 = 0；有但贵 = 1；没有 = 2。

    判读：

  • 问一高、问二低、问三低、问四低 → 现在就该试
  • 问二 = 2 → 不管别的多少分，先别用
  • 问三 = 2 → 等一致性再走一步，或者把任务拆短
  • 问四 = 2 → 你没法闭环修正，等于把 C_err 放大

    • 打完分，再用 D6 那三条判据（反事实敏感度、发散速度、规划增益）拿你自己的场景实测一遍。分数是别人的体检，自己摸的那三下才是脉。

    06

    本篇事实清单

  • 已验证（官方原文 / 论文可查）：Genie 3 的技术规格与官方自列五条局限（Google DeepMind 官方博客，2025-08-05）；Project Genie 为实验性研究原型、面向部分用户（DeepMind 2026-01 发布，光明网 2026-02-06 报道）；腾讯 HY-World 2.0 于 2026-04-16 发布并开源、支持导出 Mesh/3DGS/点云并对接 Unity、UE（央广网、上海证券报 2026-04-16 报道）；World Labs Atlas 于 2026-09-01 发布（World Labs 官方博客，中国证券报 2026-09-03 报道）；World Labs R2S2R 于 2026-07-28 发布；DayDreamer（CoRL 2022，arXiv:2206.14176，论文自报）；WBench 多轮衰减 33 分（arXiv:2605.25874，2026-05-25 提交，论文自报）
  • 厂商宣传（未见独立复现）：Atlas 的 1440p / 1 分钟 / 1–6 张图、DTU 重建误差 25.3‰；GR00T-Dreams 的 36 小时 vs 近三个月；HY-World 2.0 的"SOTA 级生成效果"
  • 不清楚：各家世界模型在真实业务流水线中的稳定产出率与人工返工比例（未见到公开数据）；Atlas 面向"部分合作伙伴早期访问"的具体名单与规模；本文不对任何产品的能力演进做预测
    • 07

    写在最后：七篇讲完，回到那个机器人

    把七篇收成一句话：世界模型输出的不是画面，是后果；真正的难题是后果在推演三十步之后还剩多少可信度；而判断它能不能用在你的场景里，看的是省下的试错够不够赔上信错的代价。

    那个倒酱油的机器人，现在可以不用练几千次了——但也不是什么都不练。它变成：在模型里练几百次，在真实世界执行几次，失败了回流修正。真实世界那几次从来没有被取消，只是被缩到了最少。

    这大概是这项技术最诚实的样子：它不消灭真实，它把真实省着用。

    七篇到此结束。最后聊个具体的：如果你的业务要用世界模型，你会把它放在流程的哪一环——最前面做原型、中间做训练数据、还是在决策前做预演？为什么是那一环？ 评论区说说你的理由。
